subject: Helios: urgent 5xx + latency surge — geo rollforward plan
messages:
From: Anna Gomez <anna@heliosfin.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: support@heliosfin.com
Date: 2028-09-04T08:12:00Z
Subject: High 5xx + latency spike impacting Helios (us-west-2 AZ2)

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and sustained tail latency starting ~07:50 PDT this morning. Our monitoring shows successful request rate for our write-heavy endpoints has dropped ~35% and p95 latency has jumped from ~120ms to ~950ms. This is hitting our payment ingestion flows — we have retries spiking and a backlog forming.

Attached a small sample of backend errors we captured and a latency heatmap. The errors are clustered to us-west-2 AZ2 (we see normal behaviour in us-west-2 AZ1 and us-east-1). Can you confirm whether there are known capacity issues or maintenance in us-west-2? We need an immediate mitigation plan; if you have a cross-region fallback we can enable it for our traffic, please advise steps and ETA.

We will need an exec update shortly (our CTO is already on standby).

Thanks,
Anna Gomez
Head of Platform Ops
Helios Financial

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: High 5xx + latency spike impacting Helios (us-west-2 AZ2)

Quick diagnostic summary (initial):
- Observed from infra metrics: error-rate jump (5xx) started at 07:46 PDT in us-west-2 AZ2.
- The batcher pool servicing Helios' high-concurrency endpoints shows continuous queue growth; a subset of inference workers are reporting elevated GC/CPU (~95%) and large KV cache pressure.
- No scheduled maintenance in the region; looks like a resource exhaustion pattern (possible kernel-level scheduling thrash) on a small number of nodes.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now:
1) Enable account-level traffic steering for Helios to prefer us-east-1 for read/write critical endpoints (critical paths only) — this will be a redispatch at the gateway layer and keep non-critical traffic in us-west-2.
   - Action plan: create routing rule 'helios-fallback-us-east-1' and set priority for customer id=67890.
   - ETA to apply: ~6 minutes to test and flip, ~12 minutes to observe stabilization.
2) Scale: increase serving-group replica count for the Helios allocation in us-west-2 by +2 temporarily to relieve batcher queues.
3) Reimage the three nodes showing repeated kernel thrash; ops will coordinate with infra.

I will run steps 1+2 immediately after we confirm approval to steer traffic. I'll post links to the monitoring slices and the runbook I'm following: https://runbooks.redwood.com/geo-rollforward-playbook and the live grafana slice (Helios > us-west-2 AZ2).

Subject: Re: High 5xx + latency spike impacting Helios (us-west-2 AZ2)

Anna — per Rishi's notes, proposed immediate plan:
- Step A (now): Apply routing rule to steer Helios critical traffic to us-east-1 for 30 minutes while we scale and remediate in us-west-2. Only critical write endpoints will be redirected; read/costly analytics remain in place so you don't pay for wide replays.
- Step B (in parallel): Autoscale +2 replicas in us-west-2 and reimage affected nodes.
- Step C: Observe for 30 minutes, run a smoke test (we will send a verification request pattern), then either peel traffic back or extend rollforward.

If you're good with this, we will: (1) place the routing rule, (2) run smoke, (3) confirm with you and your CTO for a potential credit if the disruption crosses the SLA threshold.

Draft customer-facing line for your CTO: "We're actively steering critical traffic to a healthy region (us-east-1) while we remediate the capacity issue in us-west-2. We expect service levels to return to normal within 30 minutes; Redwood will follow up with a timeline for any SLA credit as appropriate."

Please reply "approve" to proceed.

—Kimberly
